  WHY: This is documentation drift only and nothing fails at runtime, but anyone using the README to find every place the variable is read will miss the tests-main-delta copy. The source severity was NIT, mapped here to low.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:5130 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The comment on the tests-main-delta job says it "takes the head of the newest successful push or scheduled run as the base".
  WHY: The code actually uses the "head of the push or scheduled run that finished last" with the red-wins logic, so the comment misleads future maintainers. The source severity was NIT, mapped here to low. z-ai_glm-5_3-flash states that ci.yml:5129-5132 now describes the finished-last base with the red-stays-red rule.
- scripts/ci_main_delta.sh:161 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The temporary file for gh error output (read_err_file) is created but not explicitly removed on every exit path, for example when the script is interrupted during the read.
  WHY: Transient files are left in the runner's temporary directory and could accumulate if many runs are cancelled. The source severity was NIT, mapped here to low. z-ai_glm-5_3-flash notes that earlier editor and judge rounds accepted this temp-file leak on cancel as residual.

- HARDENING_SUGGESTION: .github/workflows/ci.yml, tests-main-delta, the step "Verify the final-CI merge ref is current" and the comment above it

  WHY: No fix is needed now. If the job ever runs on workflow_dispatch, give the checkout a finite fetch-depth and pass the same value to --depth. Estimated lines changed: 2. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1.
